answer: Fresh-reveal timing makes bulk fakes costly. Each epoch a beacon hands each seat a unique prompt at one unannounced instant; answers must land within a short window, so stock text cannot fit. Each reply extends a personal ledge, an unbroken hash chain to registration, so one farm cannot paste one output across seats without kinking every chain. Honest agents watch the ripple and write one short sonnet to order. A farm of N fakes needs N distinct pipelines emitting valid, chain-consistent text at once, so each extra identity costs dedicated compute, renewed each epoch.
